prompt:
Write a Python function main(env) that performs the task and returns the result. Use only env for
external operations (do not import requests, socket, subprocess or open files directly). If any stated
condition does not hold, raise an exception. env provides:
  env.http_get(url) -> {"status": int, "body": str}
  env.read_file(path) -> str
  env.write_file(path, text) -> int (characters written)
  env.run(argv: list[str]) -> str (standard output; raises if the command fails)
  env.model(model_id, prompt) -> str
Paths are relative to the working directory. The standard library (json and so on) may be imported.

Example task: Fetch https://api.example.com/weather (status must be in 200-299), JSON with a numeric "temp" that must not exceed 60. Build the text "Temp: <temp>" and write it to out/w.txt. The result is the text.
Example solution:
```python
import json


def main(env):
    resp = env.http_get("https://api.example.com/weather")
    if not 200 <= resp["status"] <= 299:
        raise RuntimeError(f"unexpected status {resp['status']}")
    temp = json.loads(resp["body"])["temp"]
    if temp > 60:
        raise RuntimeError("temp exceeds 60")
    text = f"Temp: {temp}"
    env.write_file("out/w.txt", text)
    return text
```

Task: Fetch https://api.example.com/catalog (status must be in 200-299), which returns JSON of the form {"data": {"items": [...]}}. Count the items in data.items; the count must not exceed 100. The result is the count.

Reply with only the complete solution in one ```python code block.
response:
```python
import json


def main(env):
    resp = env.http_get("https://api.example.com/catalog")
    if not 200 <= resp["status"] <= 299:
        raise RuntimeError(f"unexpected status {resp['status']}")
    data = json.loads(resp["body"])
    items = data["data"]["items"]
    if not isinstance(items, list):
        raise RuntimeError("data.items is not a list")
    count = len(items)
    if count > 100:
        raise RuntimeError("item count exceeds 100")
    return count
```
